concepts.statement: A prompt is a specification: the request states the work, the inputs that govern it, and what a good result looks like — and its quality is judged by the output's fitness for the business purpose, not by the prompt's length or its confident phrasing

Five components — role, context, task, constraints, format — carry almost every professional prompt and are run as a checklist; a role on its own changes register, not correctness, because it is one component of five

The model cannot see what exists only in the requester's head, so unstated context is the default failure: generic, on-topic output is diagnosed as a context gap before it is blamed on a model limitation
Complex work is split into ordered steps, each producing a result that can be checked before the next step consumes it — checkable intermediates are what make delegated multi-stage work diagnosable
Decomposition order is chosen by dependency and stakes: the step everything else rests on is built and verified first, because every later step inherits its errors
A single opaque prompt covering many stages cannot be diagnosed when it fails; the remedy is structural decomposition, not more instructions piled onto the same request
The output is read as a diagnostic that names which component of the request failed, and exactly one component is changed per round so the effect of the change is attributable
Iteration terminates: when successive rounds stop improving the result, the remaining gap is a task or evidence problem, and persisting with wording changes past that point is wasted effort
When definitions are already adequate and boundary cases still fail, the missing component is worked examples that mark the boundary — adding more definition is the wrong fix
Task type sets how much latitude the prompt grants: convergent work is constrained, divergent work is deliberately left open — control and range trade off, and one prompt cannot maximise both
The four named task types — analysis, research, drafting, brainstorming — are the exam's working taxonomy, and each fails in a characteristic way when the wrong prompting strategy is applied to it

Evaluation runs against three explicit references every time — the requirements, the supplied source material, and professional standards — and only the depth of review is calibrated to what is at stake, never the reference set
Completeness is a separate check from accuracy: an output can be entirely true and still omit what the decision needs, and the omission is silent — nothing present flags what is absent
Accountability is non-delegable: the sender owns every claim in what they ship regardless of who or what drafted it, and that ownership is why output evaluation carries the exam's largest weight

A hallucination is fabricated specific content — numbers, names, citations, dates — presented in the register of fact; a checkable specific bound for a consequential audience is validated against the authoritative source before it leaves your hands

Fluency, confidence and the model's own self-assessment are not accuracy signals: verification means checking a claim against an authoritative source, never against the output's register, a confidence rating, or the model's restatement of itself

Bias detection is part of routine review of ordinary outputs, not a separate exercise reserved for sensitive topics — an output can be accurate, well-formatted and still unfair, and routine review is what catches it

Pretrained knowledge carries no currency guarantee: facts that postdate the model's knowledge or change quickly are supplied or retrieved from an authoritative current source and then validated — asking the model to try harder does not create currency

Verification is cheapest when built into the request: permit an explicit "I don't know", restrict claims to the supplied sources, and require citations that can be audited — prevention at request time beats reconstruction at review time

Where numbers must be right they are computed rather than generated as prose — generation supplies language, computation supplies figures, and which of the two produced a number decides how far it can be trusted
The human-review threshold is decided in advance from four factors — stakes, reversibility, audience and regulatory exposure — not negotiated at the moment of sending under time pressure
Mandatory review means a qualified reviewer with access to the evidence; an unqualified sign-off, an evidence-blind approval or a rubber stamp does not discharge the review obligation

Adapting an output for its audience changes vocabulary, level of detail and framing while leaving the claims intact — reformatting or re-toning is never a correctness fix, and a claim that changed in adaptation needs re-verification
Comparing candidate outputs requires a stated criterion decided before reading them; without one, the most fluent candidate wins by default and the comparison is theatre

The output format — an artifact, an inline answer, or structured data — is chosen for how the result will be used and how reliably it must hold; the format that makes an error visible beats the format that reads well

An evaluation sample must represent production conditions — including missing, conflicting, stale and adversarial inputs; a clean, author-written sample proves nothing about how the work behaves in use

Inconsistency has two grains — two parts of one output disagreeing, and repeated runs disagreeing; variation is inherent to the tool, so the response is structural review and a measured consistency bound, not a bug report and not resignation
A severity-class failure is not tradable against an aggregate quality score: one prohibited error in a batch is a stop condition even when the average looks excellent

The entry point is selected before the prompt is written, because the surface determines what context is available and what the output can be — choosing it by habit rather than by task shape is the failure this decision prevents

The four named surfaces answer four different problems: chat for one-off work, Projects for recurring work with stable context, artifacts for deliverable outputs, and research mode for tasks needing current multi-source information

For occasional, human-reviewed work with no integration requirement, the interactive surface is the right answer — building automation or an agent for it is a cost with no payer, and beyond Associate scope besides

The four capability layers own four distinct jobs — Projects carry context, Skills define repeatable procedures, Code Execution verifies computation, Memory persists continuity — and the layer is chosen by which problem the task actually has

The three model tiers trade speed and cost against capability, each with a characteristic task shape: Haiku for structured high-volume work, Sonnet for most professional work, Opus for complex high-stakes work where quality outranks speed

Once several tiers clear the quality bar the task actually requires, selection is a constrained optimisation on cost and speed — the cheapest, fastest option that still meets the stated requirement wins

Defaulting to the most capable tier for everything is a cost and latency failure, not a safety margin — capability is not a free upgrade, and over-provisioning straightforward work spends both for nothing

Context is a finite budget that degrades output quality as it fills; the degradation is gradual and is easily mistaken for a model failure, which is what makes it a diagnosis to reach rather than an error to observe

The three context remedies are chosen by what must survive the transition — restart when nothing must, summarize when the conclusions must, persist when continuity must outlive the session — and the choice is made before quality visibly drops

Memory is a distinct mechanism from the conversation's context window: Memory persists continuity across sessions while the context window carries the current one, and confusing the two misroutes both configuration and diagnosis

Messy stakeholder input is turned into structured, traceable, testable requirements that others can act on — requirements analysis is the canonical delegation of analysis work, and its output is a working artefact, not a summary
A step is safe to delegate when its output can be checked: checkability, not confidence in the tool, is what makes requirements analysis and work like it a delegation candidate

Plans are built on verified numbers: the synthesis may be generated, but the figures underneath are computed — and pairing generation with computation is a design choice made when the plan is built, not a check bolted on afterwards

You cannot optimise what is not instrumented at the level where the cause lives: process optimisation starts from an instrumented workflow, so the friction being removed is the real one and not the remembered one
Design work is delegated step by step with checkpoints rather than handed over whole — each checkpoint is where human judgment re-enters, and removing them is what turns support into abdication

Iteration on a delegated design follows the same diagnostic loop as prompt iteration: the result names the component that failed, and that component — not the whole design — is what changes in the next round
Value comes from choosing which steps Claude performs: indiscriminate automation is the failure mode, because a workflow handed over whole loses the checkpoints that made it trustworthy

Each workflow step is classified against reversibility, stakes and accountability into a three-way verdict — AI-appropriate, human-retained, or collaborative — and the middle verdict is the common one
The approval gate sits after validation and before the irreversible action, and it must have a real gatekeeper: a gate placed after the action, or one nobody staffs, is not a control
A process with fixed steps and fixed validation argues for an explicit, structured workflow; autonomy is granted only where the process actually needs it, never as a default posture
Complexity in a solution design is justified by requirements, never by ambition or the appearance of rigour — the simplest design that meets the stated requirement is the professional answer

Capability claims are stated together with their limits and the human review gates that make them safe; overstating value is the stakeholder-trust failure, and accurate limits are what earn the trust back

Recognising the edge of Associate scope is itself a competency: API integration and agent building belong to a Claude Developer, enterprise architecture to a Claude Architect — the professional move is to do the in-scope part and escalate the rest, and both over-escalating and under-escalating are errors
vocabulary: Claude Architect and Claude Developer credentials

concepts.statement: Configuration is set-up-once leverage: it changes every subsequent conversation rather than a single output, and the investment is justified by how often the work recurs — which is what separates operating the tool from merely using it

Instructions govern behaviour, knowledge supplies facts, Skills define procedures, scoped Memory holds continuity — a need placed in the wrong mechanism produces a configuration that looks complete and does not hold

Every connector extends reach up to a capability edge — a request that fails at the boundary is a scope problem, not a prompt problem, and knowing each connector's edge is what prevents misrouted fixes

Uploaded knowledge needs provenance — authority, currency, scope and a review cadence — or stale and unowned content is treated as authoritative; retrieval scope is likewise a quality control, not a recall maximiser

When two knowledge authorities conflict, the resolution is by documented scope and precedence and it is stated in the output — never silently averaged, blended, or decided by which source is newer or more public
File-level metadata is not content provenance: a fresh upload timestamp says nothing about whether the content is current, and treating one as the other is how stale knowledge acquires authority

Standing instructions must be precise and testable: a vague instruction fails silently — nothing errors and nothing changes — so every instruction is written so its effect on an output can be observed

A rule that must always hold lives in trusted, durable configuration — never restated per request and never inside the material it governs, because content in uploaded or retrieved sources is data and must not acquire the authority of an instruction

Configurations decay: instructions, knowledge, Skills versions and Memory all age against a changing world, and because the decay produces no warning signal, maintenance is scheduled rather than triggered by a complaint
A configuration change that alters shared outputs is announced to the people who depend on them — informing others is part of the maintenance obligation, not a courtesy
vocabulary: Claude configurations, knowledge sources, and instructions

concepts.statement: Use cases are screened against four named criteria — reversibility, consequence, human element, accountability — and the verdict is three-way: appropriate, appropriate-with-review, or inappropriate, with the middle verdict the common one
Governance is exercised by the practitioner one decision at a time: the policy document bounds the call but does not make it, and responsible use cannot be outsourced to the existence of a policy
Data is classified before it enters a feature, and the handling is then matched to the classification — the check happens before the data moves, not after an incident

Removing or anonymising regulated identifiers before the data enters the tool is the control that lets restricted work proceed — instructing the model not to retain or misuse the data is not a control, and abandoning the task was not required

Different entry points carry different retention and handling properties — private sessions, Memory controls and connector scopes are part of where the data goes, so the destination is part of the sensitivity decision
Retention and logging scope are governed decisions: sensitive content is kept only as policy allows, and debugging convenience is not a basis for keeping secrets or identifiers in logs

Organisational policy binds even when a use looks locally harmless; the exception path runs through a named human authority with a documented process and compensating controls — not through the practitioner's own judgment of harmlessness, and never through a model's say-so
A Skill or any installed extension is software: its source and permissions are evaluated before enabling, because extending capability is a supply-chain decision, not a convenience toggle

A vendor model change or feature update enters the organisation's change-control path like any release: like-for-like comparison against a baseline, staged rollout, and a rollback path — neither auto-adopted because it is newer nor frozen forever because it is a change

When policy blocks a request, refusing well means naming the boundary, offering the permitted alternative, and following the escalation and logging policy — neither quietly complying under urgency nor decomposing the task to evade the control

Ambiguous cases are reasoned through against the stated screening criteria rather than resolved by instinct — the same four criteria decide the hard case, and the recorded reasoning is what makes the verdict defensible

Where an output affects a person's decision, disclosure of AI involvement and a route to contest the outcome belong in the design — they are due-process obligations of the workflow, not courtesies added when someone complains
Underperformance has discoverable causes, checked in a fixed order — specification, context, feature choice, configuration — cheapest and most likely first, before the tool is blamed
Naming the layer that failed is what selects the fix: prompt, context, feature choice and configuration each imply a different remedy, and a fix applied without the name is a guess
Expectation mismatch is a legitimate diagnosis: sometimes nothing is broken except the expectation, and the honest remedy is to reset what was promised rather than to keep tuning what was delivered
Attribution requires a reconstructed baseline and one changed variable at a time — changing several things at once, or one thing with no baseline, destroys the diagnosis while reading as decisiveness

A refusal is diagnosed against the task, current policy and permissions, and recent changes; the permitted portion is then redesigned and done, or the work is escalated — evading or stripping the control is never the fix
A disappointing output is evidence: the critique is translated into one specific adjustment, not a general resolve to do better — and the adjustment targets the component the critique names
A fix that worked is captured as an instruction or a Skill so it persists beyond the session — an unrecorded fix is re-derived on every future occurrence, which is decay by another name

Optimisation is deliberate and measured — instrument the workflow, find the friction, promote the fix into configuration, measure the gain; optimising without a baseline produces an unfalsifiable claim of improvement
